rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this candidate raises obfuscation pressure while still shielding the hot recursive/numeric kernels (tak, takFP, fib, fibFP, fannkuch, spectral-norm) from expensive transforms. SUB and SPLIT get the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights because they carry near-zero runtime and correctness risk and can be applied everywhere, including inner loops. FLA and BCF get strong security weights but suppressed RuntimeCost weights so the selector avoids stacking them onto the hottest recursion- and loop-dominated functions, where bogus control flow and flattening cost the most; with only 721 bytes of text there is ample size budget, so SizeCost stays low except where it correlates with runtime-heavy code. IBR and ICALL are kept at moderate security weights to add indirection-based diversity on the call-heavy benchmark functions without inflating the RuntimeCost pull on hot paths. IGV is deliberately down-weighted (low SecurityGain, elevated CorrectnessRisk 0.3) because this benchmark set has almost no global variable traffic, so its benefit is marginal while indirect-global lowering carries the highest miscompile risk of the seven passes.
